## Final answer

**Dentate gyrus** is the tissue in which bad responders show the highest number of significantly differentially expressed genes (lfc > 0.5 and basemean > 10) compared to controls: **303 genes**, versus 146 in baseline blood and 97 in final blood. The ranking is robust: dentate gyrus also wins under the stricter padj < 0.05 variant (194 vs 88 vs 15) and under the both-directions |lfc| > 0.5 variant (410 vs 194 vs 194).

## Evidence (executed script: analysis_bix9_q5.py)

Parsed NormCount: 25,402 unique gene rows × 188 cols. Used the bad_responder-vs-Control DESeq blocks (Comp2/Comp5/Comp8, group A = bad, B = control, lfc = log2(bad/control)):

| Tissue | n genes | lfc NA | PRIMARY: lfc>0.5 & basemean>10 | + padj<0.05 | \|lfc\|>0.5 & basemean>10 | \|lfc\|>0.5 + padj<0.05 | down only (lfc<−0.5) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| baseline_blood | 25,402 | 5,224 | **146** | 88 | 194 | 93 | 48 |
| dentate_gyrus | 25,402 | 3,860 | **303** | 194 | 410 | 245 | 107 |
| final_blood | 25,402 | 5,939 | **97** | 15 | 194 | 21 | 97 |

Direction sanity checks passed: mean baseMeanA(bad) vs baseMeanB(control) per tissue (e.g., DG 766.3 vs 768.4 — near-equal means with tissue-specific lfc patterns), and the authors' DEG 'U' flag was previously verified to equal padj<0.05 & lfc>0.5 in all three blocks. Example primary-set genes (dentate gyrus): 1700003F12Rik, 1700007I08Rik, 1700016K19Rik, 1700034J05Rik, 2810417H13Rik.

Artifacts: `analysis_bix9_q5.py` (executed script) and `output/per_tissue_deg_counts.csv` (results table).
